name: HD 131399

planets.name: Ab
planets.note: Wagner et al. (2016) claimed HD 131399 Ab as a ~4 Mjup, ~850 K planet on a wide (~82 au) orbit within the hierarchical triple HD 131399ABC - the first planet imaged in such a system. Common-proper-motion tests from new Gemini/GPI epochs plus reanalyzed VLT/SPHERE and Keck data (Nielsen et al. 2017) showed the source is a slow-moving background star, refuting the planet interpretation. Wagner et al. (2022, the Scorpion Planet Survey) independently re-confirmed the background-star nature from the relative position-angle vs. time trend (their Fig. 4).

extra_papers.title: Evidence That the Directly Imaged Planet HD 131399 Ab Is a Background Star

images.note: GPI cADI images at four 2017 epochs (J/H/K1); combined with reanalyzed SPHERE+Keck astrometry these show the object does not share the primary's proper motion - it is a stationary background star.

paper.title: Evidence That the Directly Imaged Planet HD 131399 Ab Is a Background Star

notes: Young A1V star in Upper Centaurus-Lupus (Sco-Cen), primary of the hierarchical triple HD 131399ABC. Host of the refuted directly-imaged planet candidate Ab, later shown to be a background star. A separate close stellar companion to HD 131399A was independently detected in HARPS radial velocities (Lagrange et al. 2017).
